links.outcome: NLP labeling error rates compared across age, sex, and race/ethnicity subgroups
links.effect: Error rates differed across age groups (P<.001) for all tools except RRA on MIMIC; highest for CheXpert, RRA, cTAKES in patients >80 years (mean 15.8% ± 5.0); GPT-4 highest at ages 60-80 (8.3%).
links.quote: Differences (P < .001) in error rates were observed across age groups for all NLP tools except RRA on the MIMIC dataset, with the highest error rates for CheXpert, RRA, and cTAKES in patients older than 80 years (mean, 15.8% ± 5.0) and the highest error rate for GPT-4 in patients 60-80 years of age (8.3%).

links.outcome: Performance differences across patient demographic subgroups
links.effect: Aggregate accuracy was high (88.7%-94.3% on MIMIC/IU for most tools), but subgroup analyses showed significant bias with poorer performance in older patients.
links.quote: Although commonly used NLP tools for chest radiograph report annotation are accurate when evaluating reports in aggregate, demographic subanalyses showed significant bias, with poorer performance in older patients.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating accuracy and demographic bias (equity audit) of four NLP tools (including GPT-4) on labeling radiology reports across age, sex, and race/ethnicity subgroups.
